title: At least eight dead after Brooklyn apartment building collapses into construction pit
excerpt: At least eight people were killed after a three-story Brooklyn apartment building collapsed into a construction pit next door, with rescue crews still searching the rubble.
content:
At least eight people were confirmed dead early Thursday after a three-story apartment building in Brooklyn collapsed into an open construction pit next door, and rescue crews were still searching the rubble for survivors.

The building at 1321 Flatbush Ave., in the Flatbush section of Brooklyn, fell into the construction site next door at 2625 Bedford Ave. shortly after 4 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 11. The Fire Department of New York said it received the call at 4:01 p.m. and units arrived within one minute.

The death toll rose through the morning. Six bodies were pulled from the rubble overnight, and two more people died after being taken to a hospital, the New York Post reported early Thursday. On Wednesday night, officials had confirmed two deaths and 17 injuries.

At least 19 other people were injured, four of them critically, according to the Post's updated reporting. Seven children were among the injured. Firefighters pulled several survivors from the wreckage alive Wednesday evening, including a woman and her two children, ages 7 and 2, and a pregnant woman. At least three firefighters were injured during the rescue effort.

More than 250 fire and emergency medical workers responded, with 69 units and search dogs working the pile. Fire Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore said Wednesday night that crews did not know how many people might still be in the collapse zone, and officials warned the toll would likely keep rising. The search was expected to stretch for days.

The building was a three-story mixed-use structure with a store at street level and four apartments above it. The lot next door was being prepared for a new building: city Department of Buildings filings show a January 2026 application for a nine-story mixed-use building with a cellar, filed for the owner, W6 Facility X LLC. Buildings Commissioner Ahmed Tigani said construction crews had been excavating the site next door when the building crumbled into it.

Officials have not given a cause. The Department of Buildings and law enforcement agencies are investigating, and Mayor Zohran Mamdani joined city officials at a late-night briefing. The records do not explain the collapse, and officials have not tied it to the work at the site.

Displaced residents were taken to a reception center at the Flatbush YMCA, 1401 Flatbush Ave., where the Red Cross registered 12 adults and helped find places for them to spend the night. Flatbush Avenue was closed between Clarendon Avenue and Bedford Avenue while rescue work continued.
